title.en: Notes service: a slow read writes a stale note back into the cache
title.ja: ノートサービス：遅い読み取りが古いノートをキャッシュに書き戻す

lede.en: GET reads the cache, falls back to the database and fills the cache; PATCH writes the database, then deletes the cache key. If a PATCH lands between a GET's database read and its cache fill, the cache keeps the old note until the TTL of {{cache_ttl}} runs out.
lede.ja: GET はキャッシュを読み、なければデータベースを読んでキャッシュを埋める。PATCH はデータベースを書いてからキャッシュキーを削除する。GET の読み取りとキャッシュ書き込みの間に PATCH が入ると、TTL {{cache_ttl}} が切れるまで古いノートが残る。

second_delete_delay.basis: Longer than the slowest GET between its database read and its cache fill; a proposal, not in the code.

e-no-version-check.absent: a version check or lock between the database read and the cache fill

scenarios.title: Cold read fills the cache, the next read hits

steps.t: Read the note from the database
Fill the cache with a TTL of {{cache_ttl}}
The next read is a cache hit

scenarios.title: A PATCH lands between a GET's read and its cache fill

steps.t: Reader's GET reads the old note
steps.d: The request now holds the old note in memory; nothing ties it to the row's current state.

steps.t: Editor's PATCH writes the new note
PATCH deletes the cache key and replies
steps.d: The key is already absent, so this delete changes nothing.

steps.t: Reader's GET fills the cache with the old note
steps.d: The stale value enters the cache here, after the only delete has already run.

steps.t: Every later read hits the stale entry until the TTL ends
do: Stale for up to {{cache_ttl}} after the fill.

scenarios.title: The GET fills the cache only if the note is unchanged since its read

steps.t: Reader's GET skips the fill: the note changed after its read
steps.d: The fill compares the note it read with the row as it is now; the PATCH changed the row, so nothing is written and the cache stays empty.

steps.t: Reader gets the note it read, once
steps.d: This one response is as old as the read; no later read sees it.

steps.t: The next read misses and caches the new note

options.label: Fill the cache only if the row is unchanged since the read
pros: No stale window: a fill that lost the race is dropped
The PATCH handler does not change
cons: Needs an atomic compare in the cache client, or a version to compare
A dropped fill sends the next read to the database again

options.label: Delete the key again after a delay
pros: Two lines in the PATCH handler
cons: A stale window of up to {{second_delete_delay}} remains
The delay is a guess about the slowest GET

options.label: Keep the code, rely on the TTL
cons: Stale for up to {{cache_ttl}} after every unlucky PATCH

decision.deciding_factor: It removes the stale window instead of shortening it, for one compare per fill.
decision.revisit_when: The compare adds visible latency to a fill, or the cache cannot compare atomically.

checks.q: The PATCH already deleted the key. What does the cache hold after this step?
checks.answer: The old note, v1: the GET fills the cache after the only delete ran.

checks.q: Same moment, with the fix: does the GET write its old note into the cache?
checks.answer: No. The row changed since the read, so the fill is skipped and the cache stays empty.
